S6.01.note: No in-app colour control was found; the colours come from the editor theme.
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar.
Open the Command Palette and switch the editor colour theme to a light theme, then to a dark theme.
Check that the panel page background and the raised panels change together with the editor theme.
S6.01.where: AGI Code panel background, seen through the editor theme

steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Click the + button labelled Attach or use tools under the message box.
Compare the menu surface with the panel page behind it; it should look raised and distinct.
S6.02.where: The Add context menu surface, opened from the + button

labels.text: Include text files in your next message

steps: Click the + button labelled Attach or use tools under the message box.
Compare the bold item titles, such as Attach workspace files, with the grey description under each one.
Check that both are easy to read against the menu background.
S6.03.where: Text colours inside the Add context menu

steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Look at the border around the message box whose placeholder reads Describe a task…
Open the + menu and compare its border with the message box border.
S6.04.where: Border lines around the message box and menus

S6.05.note: The highlight is set by the arrow keys in the slash menu code.
steps: Click the / button labelled Commands under the message box.
Press the Down arrow key once.
Check that the highlighted item has a clear fill and readable text.
S6.05.where: Highlight colour of the selected item in the Commands menu

S6.06.note: No single fixed control was found that always shows a status message; the tester needs an action that produces one.
steps: Trigger an error or warning message in the panel, such as sending a message with no sign-in or API key.
Compare the red or yellow status text and its background with the normal panel text.
S6.06.where: Success, warning, error and info colours on status messages

S6.07.note: The font comes from the editor setting; the app has no font control of its own.
steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Compare the panel text font with the font in an open code editor tab.
Confirm the panel uses the editor's UI font.
S6.07.where: Font family of the panel text, which follows the editor font setting

S6.08.note: The page title Settings is in the settings page; the heading levels are only partly visible in the settings page.
steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Click the gear button titled Settings in the panel header.
Click General in the left list.
Compare the Model and reasoning card heading with the page title Settings and the other card headings.
S6.08.where: Settings button at the top of the AGI Code panel > General

S6.09.note: The app reads the editor font size and offers no text-size control of its own; no in-app text-size preference was found.
steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Change the editor font size in the editor settings.
Check that the panel body text grows or shrinks with it.
S6.09.where: Body text size in the panel, which follows the editor font size

labels.text: Include text files in your next message

steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Click the + button labelled Attach or use tools under the message box.
Look at the small grey text under each item title, such as the text under Attach workspace files.
Check that the small text is readable and not smaller than about 12 pixels.
S6.10.where: + button (Attach or use tools) > Attach workspace files

S6.11.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account or an API key (the reply needs one)
steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Click the message box with the placeholder Describe a task….
Type a request that asks for a short code sample and send it.
Look at the code in the reply and compare its font with the normal reply text.
S6.11.where: Message box (Describe a task…) > send a request that gets a code reply

S6.12.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account or an API key (the reply needs one)
steps: Send a request that gets a multi-line reply in AGI Code.
Read the reply and check that the lines are evenly spaced and easy to read.
S6.12.where: Line spacing inside replies and settings text

S6.13.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account or an API key (the reply needs one)
steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Click the message box with the placeholder Describe a task….
Send a request that asks for two short paragraphs.
Check the gap between the two paragraphs in the reply.
S6.13.where: Message box (Describe a task…) > send a message that gets a reply with two paragraphs

S6.14.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account or an API key (the reply needs one)
steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Click the message box with the placeholder Describe a task….
Send a request that asks for a bulleted list with one nested item.
Check the indent of the list and the step in from the parent item to the nested item.
S6.14.where: Message box (Describe a task…) > send a message that gets a bulleted list reply

S6.15.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account or an API key (the reply needs one)
steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Click the message box with the placeholder Describe a task….
Send a request that asks for a short code block.
Check the space inside the code block between its edge and the code text.
S6.15.where: Message box (Describe a task…) > send a message that gets a code block reply

S6.16.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account or an API key (the reply needs one)
steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Click the message box with the placeholder Describe a task….
Send a request that asks for a small table with three columns.
Check the padding inside each table cell and that the cell spacing is even.
S6.16.where: Message box (Describe a task…) > send a message that gets a table reply

S6.17.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account or an API key (the reply needs one)
steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Click the message box with the placeholder Describe a task….
Send one message, wait for the reply, then send a second message.
Compare the vertical gap between the first turn and the second turn.
S6.17.where: Message box (Describe a task…) > send two messages in a row

S6.18.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account or an API key (the reply needs one)
S6.18.note: The row is hidden until hover in the stylesheet, so it may need a mouse move to appear.
steps: Send a message and wait for the reply to finish.
Move the mouse over the reply.
Look at the row of small buttons that appears under it, such as the one titled Regenerate.
Compare the gap between the bottom of the reply and that row with the other spacing in the reply.
S6.18.where: Under a finished reply > Regenerate button (appears on hover)

steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Look at the space between the edge of the message box whose placeholder reads Describe a task… and its inner text and buttons.
Type a long message and check the padding stays even.
S6.19.where: Space around the message box and its + and / buttons at the bottom of the panel

S6.20.note: The panel width drag is done with the mouse on the VS Code sidebar border.
steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Drag the edge of the AGI Code panel to make it narrower, then wider.
Check the space between the panel edge and the chat content, which should step as the width changes.
S6.20.where: Side space (gutter) of the chat content, which changes with panel width

steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Click the button titled Sessions in the panel header.
Look at the list of sessions in the Sessions sheet.
Compare the height of each session row, and check that all rows have the same height.
S6.21.where: Sessions button at the top of the AGI Code panel > session list

steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Click the + button labelled Attach or use tools.
Look at the height of each item in the Add context menu.
Press Escape, click the / button labelled Commands, and compare its item height with the + menu items.
S6.22.where: + button (Attach or use tools) > menu items; also / button (Commands)

S6.23.note: The only dialog found is the onboarding dialog titled Work with your code (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts), opened by sidebarProvider.showOnboarding; I did not find the user action that calls it, so its trigger is unverified.

steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Click the gear button titled Settings in the panel header.
Click Runtime in the left list.
Look at the label AGI CLI path and its input box, then the label Open chat in below it.
Compare the gap between the label and its input with the gap between fields.
S6.24.where: Settings button at the top of the AGI Code panel > Runtime

steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Look at the row of icon buttons at the top right of the panel.
Hover over each icon and read its tooltip: Sessions, Settings, New chat.
Compare the icon sizes and line thickness across the three icons.
S6.25.where: Header icon buttons at the top of the AGI Code panel: Sessions, Settings, New chat

S6.26.needs: a signed-in account with at least one session
S6.26.note: Sizes come from the control-sm, control-md and control-lg tokens in webviewContent.ts (lines 225-227); the settings webview also defines them. Visual size match was not checked on screen.
steps: Open the AGI Code side panel from the left activity bar.
Look at the three square icon buttons at the top of the panel (Sessions, Settings, New chat) and note they are the same size.
Click Sessions and hover a session row to show its small icon buttons on the right.
Compare the small row buttons (24px) with the header buttons (28px): one defined set of sizes, as Expected.
S6.26.where: AGI Code side panel > header buttons Sessions, Settings, New chat (28px squares); then Sessions > hover a session row for its small icon buttons

S6.27.note: Radius tokens are defined in the shared design-tokens package (agiCornerCssVars), applied in webviewContent.ts (line 214) and settingsWebviewContent.ts (line 136). No control sets them.
steps: Open the AGI Code side panel and look at the composer box, the plus menu (+) and the model menu.
Compare the corner rounding across them: they should come from a small set of radius steps, as Expected.
S6.27.where: Corner rounding on the composer card, menus and session rows in the AGI Code side panel

S6.28.note: Shadows are two tokens (elevation-2 and elevation-3, webviewContent.ts lines 218-219) built on the VS Code widget shadow colour, so they follow the host theme.
steps: Open the AGI Code side panel and click the + button labelled Attach or use tools.
Look at the edge of the menu that opens: it should sit above the chat with a soft shadow that differs from the page.
Click the Auto model button (title Model) and compare its popover shadow with the plus menu.
Switch VS Code between a light and a dark colour theme and check the shadows still show.
S6.28.where: AGI Code side panel > Attach or use tools (+ button, bottom left of the composer)

S6.29.note: The layer ladder is the z-content, z-dropdown, z-popover, z-overlay and z-sheet tokens at webviewContent.ts lines 220-224.
steps: Open a conversation with several messages and click the + button so its menu opens over the messages.
Scroll the chat behind the open menu and check the menu stays on top.
Click Sessions and check the Sessions sheet covers the chat above the composer.
Compare with Expected: the layers stack in one order and nothing overlaps wrongly.
S6.29.where: Stacking in the AGI Code side panel: the plus menu and model popover over the chat, and the Sessions sheet over the panel

S6.30.needs: a signed-in account that can send a message
S6.30.note: Durations and curves are tokens (duration-spin 1000ms, duration-pulse 1200ms, webviewContent.ts lines 215 and 382). Exact timing was not measured on screen.
steps: Open the AGI Code side panel and hover over the header buttons and the Send button to see the quick colour fade.
Send a short message and watch the loading indicator while the reply runs.
Compare the speed and easing of the fades and spinner with Expected: one set of named durations and curves.
S6.30.where: Motion in the AGI Code side panel: hover colour changes, the loading spinner while a reply runs, and the pulse

S6.31.needs: a Mac with the Reduce motion setting available
S6.31.note: There is no in-app motion setting; the only control is the macOS Reduce motion switch, which the webview reads through the prefers-reduced-motion media query (webviewContent.ts line 2774; settingsWebviewContent.ts line 1254).
steps: Turn on macOS Reduce motion (System Settings > Accessibility > Display). This is outside the app.
Open the AGI Code side panel and send a message.
Watch the loading spinner: it should stop looping after one turn rather than keep spinning, as Expected.
S6.31.where: Looping and travelling motion in the AGI Code side panel stops or turns gentle when macOS Reduce motion is on

S6.32.needs: a signed-in account with a chat that includes a code block
S6.32.note: The app has no light, dark or system choice of its own: the surface uses VS Code's theme tokens with AGI fallbacks (webviewContent.ts lines 190 and 254). The follow-the-system option is VS Code's own theme setting and was not checked. Code block colours were not verified on screen.
steps: Open VS Code and set a light colour theme, then open the AGI Code side panel.
Switch to a dark colour theme with the same panel open.
Check the panel, the composer and a code block in the chat all change together, as Expected.
S6.32.where: Colours of the whole AGI Code side panel follow the VS Code colour theme (light or dark)

S6.33.needs: VS Code with a high contrast theme available
S6.33.note: A forced-colors block exists at webviewContent.ts line 2783, but forced colours are a Windows high-contrast mode and may not switch on for a Mac tester. The in-app effect is reached only through VS Code's theme.
steps: Set VS Code to a high contrast colour theme (outside the app).
Open the AGI Code side panel and look at the header buttons and the composer border.
Press Tab through the header buttons and check the focus outline is clear, as Expected.
S6.33.where: Stronger text, borders and focus in the AGI Code side panel when VS Code uses a high-contrast colour theme

S6.34.note: Hover, pressed and disabled rules are in webviewContent.ts lines 553 and 213; the selected state is shown on the Sessions tabs.
steps: Open the AGI Code side panel and move the pointer over the Settings button; the hover state should show.
Press and hold the Settings button; the pressed state should show, then release.
Press Tab to move focus to the buttons and check the focus ring.
With the composer empty, look at the Send button: it should look disabled. Type text and check it looks active, as Expected.
S6.34.where: AGI Code side panel > header button Settings (hover, press), and the composer Send button (disabled when empty)

S6.35.note: The activity bar uses media/agi-symbol.png and the extension uses media/icon.png (package.json lines 84 and 958). The pixel sizes against the platform needs were not checked.
steps: Look at the left activity bar in VS Code and find the AGI Code icon.
Zoom or compare it with the Extensions view listing for the AGI Code extension.
Check the icon is sharp and matches the brand mark used in the panel, as Expected.
S6.35.where: VS Code left activity bar > AGI Code icon (title AGI Code); the extension icon is in the Extensions view
